verdict.rationale: Twenty's own docs say developers can create custom objects, add custom fields with 20+ field types, and build relations between any objects, including many-to-many. Custom objects get first-class API endpoints, views and permissions, and schema can be managed programmatically via the Metadata API or defined as code via the CLI. A community report calls the customization promising, though it does not corroborate hands-on depth. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of custom object and relationship modeling depth.

support.subject: As a developer, I can model custom objects with fields and relationships beyond the built-in contacts, companies, and deals

citations.quote: Create custom objects, add custom fields with 20+ field types, and build relationships between any objects.
You can create custom relations between any objects, including many-to-many relationships.
Schema management: create/modify/delete objects, fields, and relations. This is how you programmatically change your data model.
Define objects, fields, and views as code
Custom objects get the same first-class treatment as built-in ones — including API endpoints, views, permissions, and workflow triggers.
